O R D E R Delay condoned in Diary No.14076/2024.
Leave granted.
The appellants are before this Court aggrieved by the rejection of their applications, filed under Section 389 Cr.P.C., by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur.

entities.text: High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellants were convicted of offences punishable under Sections 366, 342, 376(2)(n) read with Section 109, and Section 506 Part-II of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The maximum sentence imposed upon them is rigorous imprisonment for a period of 20 years along with payment of fines.

Their appeals against such conviction are pending before the High Court of Madhya Pradesh and, in the meanwhile, they sought suspension of their Reason: sentences and grant of bail pending disposal of their appeals.
However, by the orders impugned before us, the High Court disallowed their prayer.

While so,
respondent No.2 in the appeal filed by Raju Rathore, who is none other than the victim, filed an affidavit stating that she is the lawfully wedded wife of accused No.1 in the case, who allegedly committed rape upon her with the abetment of the appellants herein.
She further stated that she bore two children out of such wedlock.

Mr. Abhimanyu Singh, learned counsel for the State of Madhya Pradesh, was thereupon requested to obtain instructions in that regard by deputing a responsible Police Officer to visit the victim and ascertain the factual position.

sentences.text: Today, Mr. Abhimanyu Singh, learned counsel, would state that a responsible Police Officer did visit the victim and she confirmed what was stated in the affidavit filed before this Court.
In that view of the matter, there is no necessity to continue with the incarceration of the appellants pending the disposal of their appeals.

The appeals are accordingly allowed, suspending the sentence imposed upon the appellants in ST Case No.80/2019 on the file of the II Additional Sessions Judge, Anuppur,
District Anuppur, Madhya Pradesh, and directing their release on bail pending disposal of the appeals on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the trial Court.
